item.title: Spurs' Julian Champagnie brings Halloween cheer to hospitalized children
item.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie poses for a photo with a family during a visit to Methodist Children's Hospital in San Antonio, Texas Friday, October 30, 2026. (Photo by Reginald Thomas II/San Antonio Spurs) (Reginald Thomas II/ San Antonio Spurs/Methodist Healthcare) Julian Champagnie traded his jersey for a Shrek costume during a surprise Halloween visit to Methodist Children's Hospital on Friday. Champagnie was joined by the Spurs Coyote as he went door-to-door visiting children hospitalized at Methodist. He exchanged high fives, posed for photos, signed autographs, and passed out treats to patients who can't participate in traditional trick-or-treating this year. Felicia Barrera, the mother of a patient at Methodist Children's Hospital, said Champagnie's visit brought "smiles, laughter, and the Spurs magic to brighten up" an unexpected Halloween stay in the hospital. READ MORE : How Spurs' chemistry contributed to Julian Champagnie's big night "For a minute it helps you forget why you're here and not see your kid in pain and I can't thank them enough for that small distraction," she added. This was the Spurs forward's second year participating in Methodist's reverse trick-or-treating, where hospital staff bring spooky cheer directly to patients' rooms. Last year, he dressed as Scooby Doo to pass out Spurs swag and candy to children in the hospital. "That's what this is for," Champagnie said in a press release. "To come out here and give the kids and their parents a good time, spread some joy and make them smile a little. Every time I get to come out here and make kids smile, it makes me happy." item.description: Silva the saviour as Dortmund rally late to draw with Bayern Munich MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ) In their 141st-ever meeting Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund played out and exciting and dramatic 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena this evening. The Bavarian giants looked to have held out for parity until Fabio Silva arrived off the bench to secure BVB a point. On top of an already raucous atmosphere before a ball was kicked, Harry Kane walked out to a hero’s reception. The Englishman raised his recently acquired Ballon d’Or aloft and thanked everyone for their support. Then it was down to business. Both teams had early spells of possession, but Bayern looked more threatening in comparison. The first notable chance fell the way of the hosts, Alphonso Davies managed to burrow his way into the box. A kind deflection sat up nicely for Michael Olise, catching his half-volley sweetly. The post came to a rooted Gregor Kobel’s rescue. Dortmund also has a sniff at goal, but Bayern’s rearguard remained defiant in protecting Jonas Urbig. That changed swiftly midway through the half when Bayern’s shot-stopper produced a fine parry low to his right to stop Jobe Bellingham. item.title: Simon Harmer and Rabada dismantle Australia in Cape Town; South Africa storm to 2-1 series win
item.description: South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs in the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town on Saturday to win the three-match series 2-1. Off-spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16, while Kagiso Rabada became the fastest bowler by balls bowled to reach 350 Test wickets. Chasing a target of 288, Australia were bowled out for 111 in the second session on the final day. The result also took South Africa above Australia to the top of the Test world rankings for the first time since January 2016. The Proteas rallied from 1-0 down in the first test series between the teams in South Africa since the " Sandpapergate ” scandal in 2018. Australia had won the first test in Durban by 214 runs, and South Africa won the second test in Gqeberha by an innings and 31 runs. Australia's hopes of completing the chase suffered an early setback as they lost two wickets in the first over. Rabada struck with the new ball, removing the top three batters to leave the visitors struggling at 62/8. Harmer then took charge, claiming all of the last six wickets to finish with figures of 6-16 in 21.1 overs. He ended the match with 10 wickets for 120 runs, his first 10-wicket haul in Test cricket. — SuperSportTV (@SuperSportTV) Rabada finished with 3-39 in the second innings and reached the 350-wicket mark in 13,808 deliveries. He became the fastest bowler to achieve the milestone by balls bowled, going past South Africa's Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan's Waqar Younis (14,905). Rabada dismissed opener Matt Renshaw for a duck, with wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton taking the catch down the leg side. He then trapped Marnus Labuschagne (4) leg before wicket in the same over before Marco Jansen caught Travis Head at gully to leave Australia in trouble. First-innings centurion Josh Inglis was run out for four while attempting a quick single, adding to Australia's problems. Harmer then took the remaining wickets. Nathan Lyon was top scorer for Australia and remained unbeaten on 33. He and captain Pat Cummins, who scored 11 off 90 balls, added 45 runs for the ninth wicket, the highest partnership of the innings. The stand lasted 17.2 overs before Harmer dismissed Cummins leg before wicket and bowled Josh Hazlewood to seal the win. 135405470 The partnership also helped Australia avoid being bowled out for less than 100 in consecutive Tests, something that had last happened during the 1936-37 Ashes. Cameron Green was the only batter among Australia's top eight to face at least 30 deliveries, scoring 27 off 110 balls. The defeat is likely to raise questions about Australia's batting and their decision to bowl on the first day morning, which left them chasing a target in the fourth innings on a wearing pitch. The victory also keeps South Africa's hopes of defending their World Test Championship title alive. They had beaten Australia in the previous WTC final at Lord's in 2025.

item.title: Brighton stun Man City, 10-man Man Utd beaten by Chelsea
item.description: Brighton beat Manchester City away for the first time in the club's history (Darren Staples) Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday, while Manchester United slumped to another damaging defeat for Michael Carrick at Chelsea. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler's men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad. This time they held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. "We expected a game where we had to suffer. Coming to this place is very difficult, facing one of the best teams in the world," said Hurzeler. "I'm really proud of how my players stuck together. They had a little bit of luck but, in the end, deserved it." City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. "In this moment we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid," said Maresca. "I think we did enough to deserve something but we need to move on and try to win games." Defeat for City means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. - Man Utd self-implode - Manchester United's nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period. Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring. Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty. Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four. "The two halves of football couldn't probably be further apart," said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday's Champions League tie against Roma. "We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half." item.title: PREVIEW: Arsenal chase first Anfield league win since 2012
item.description: PREVIEW: Arsenal chase first Anfield league win since 2012 Liverpool welcome defending champions Arsenal to Anfield for Sunday’s blockbuster Premier League clash, hoping to halve the six-point gap between the sides. Arsenal moved level on 21 points with Manchester City following a 2-0 victory over Everton at the Emirates, with both goals coming from their centre-backs. Ezri Konsa put the Gunners ahead after just seven minutes before Gabriel Magalhães doubled their lead with a second-half header. Liverpool recorded a similar result in their latest Premier League outing, beating Brighton 2-0 at Anfield. Four minutes after Pascal Groß’s own goal, Alexander Isak turned home first time from Bradley Barcola’s cross. The Reds saw out the victory to clinch their first home league win of the season and keep their fourth league clean sheet. Liverpool and Arsenal had very different nights in their midweek Carabao Cup ties, with both matches finishing 1-1 before going to penalties. Iraola’s side progressed to the quarter-finals after edging Chelsea 6-5 in the shootout. Arteta’s side, meanwhile, suffered a shock exit to League Two Fleetwood Town, losing 5-3 on penalties. Despite their Carabao Cup elimination, Arsenal have made a strong start to their Premier League title defence. The Gunners have won seven of their opening eight league fixtures, conceding only five goals and keeping five clean sheets. Since their heavy 3-0 home defeat to Man City, Liverpool have won five consecutive games across all competitions. Alexander Isak has also impressed in front of goal, sitting second in the top-flight scoring charts with six goals, behind Erling Haaland. Arsenal haven’t beaten Liverpool on their home ground in the top flight since September 2012, with their subsequent 13 league visits producing five draws and eight defeats. Their last meeting at Anfield, on 31 August 2025, ended in a 1-0 victory for the hosts, while the return match at the Emirates on 8 January 2026 finished goalless. Liverpool remain the only club to have prevented the Gunners from scoring in both Premier League fixtures during the 2025/26 season. Iraola’s side will be without Jeremie Frimpong , but Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz could return for Sunday’s clash. As for the visitors, Bukayo Saka is still sidelined following an injury sustained against Bayern Munich , while Noni Madueke remains a doubt for the trip to Merseyside. However, Arteta could welcome back Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis , with all three back in training ahead of the game. The hosts will be aiming to extend their unbeaten home run against Arsenal in the league, while the Gunners could go top of the Premier League with at least a draw after Man City’s defeat to Brighton on Saturday. The match kicks off on Sunday, 1 November, at 16:30 GMT.

item.title: Ireland's Indian-origin pacer Jai Moondra creates cricket history with record-breaking 6/26 bowling figures
item.description: Ireland fast bowler Jai Moondra created history with an outstanding performance against Namibia in the fourth ODI of the five-match series on Friday. The 29-year-old took six wickets for just 26 runs in his 10 overs, helping Ireland defend their total of 298 runs and secure a convincing 130-run victory at the High Performance Oval in Windhoek. Moondra’s remarkable bowling performance also helped him set a new record for Ireland in international cricket. He became the country's most successful bowler in terms of wickets taken and runs conceded in a single international innings. Before Moondra’s achievement, the record for Ireland’s best bowling figures belonged to Josh Little, who took six wickets for 36 runs in 10 overs against Zimbabwe in Harare on December 15, 2023. Moondra bettered those figures by conceding 10 fewer runs while taking the same number of wickets. The Indian-origin fast bowler, who made his international debut for Ireland earlier this year in a T20I against India, is now the third Irish player to take a six-wicket haul in ODIs and the fifth to achieve the feat in international cricket. Andy McBrine remains the only Irish bowler to have taken more than one six-wicket haul in ODIs. Second-best bowling figures against Namibia Moondra’s performance also ranks as the second-best bowling effort against Namibia in international cricket. Australia's Glenn McGrath holds the top spot after taking seven wickets for 15 runs in seven overs during the 2003 ODI World Cup match against Namibia in Potchefstroom. Meanwhile, Ireland’s victory helped the team level the five-match ODI series 2-2. Both sides will now meet in the series-deciding fifth ODI in Windhoek on Sunday, November 1.

item.title: Maresca's big test is to address mounting Man City issues
item.description: Enzo Maresca enjoyed a flawless start as Manchester City manager, winning his first seven Premier League games in charge, but the honeymoon period is now over. Having lost at Aston Villa last weekend, City have now suffered back-to-back top-flight defeats after being beaten 1-0 at home by Brighton on Saturday. "A bit strange," Maresca said of the result. "It is the same feeling as after Aston Villa away. We did enough to deserve something more but we have to move on and try to win games. "We created a good volume of offensive action. Sometimes you have to be more clinical and score but it's important that we create. "We did everything to be honest. The attitude was good, I have nothing to say about that or the performance. The players fought until the end and hopefully next time we are more lucky." Maresca seemed to slot in seamlessly after taking on the seemingly impossible job of replacing the legendary Pep Guardiola, but now needs to find solutions to City's stuttering form. With chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano keeping a close eye on proceedings at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, the City manager has issues to address across the pitch. Brighton stun Man City to maintain bright start Defensive errors proving costly City missed out on the title to Arsenal last season and are expected to be the closest challengers again. Maresca's men remain top on goal difference but will be overtaken by the Gunners if they beat Liverpool on Sunday (kick-off 16:30 GMT). City have conceded 10 goals in nine league games this term - double the amount that Mikel Arteta's men have let in. Individual errors at the back are beginning to stack up - Marc Guehi, who was dropped for this game, and Gianluigi Donnarumma were culpable at Villa Park and Matheus Nunes was the guilty party against Brighton. Maresca has been unequivocal about his number one, saying it is "Donnarumma plus 10" on the teamsheet but defensive frailties mean City have now kept only one clean sheet in their past eight games in all competitions. The result also meant City lost consecutive Premier League games for the first time in 14 months. "Why?" Maresca asked of the individual errors. "Sometimes it happens. "Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football. It happens many times against us. "We need to analyse what we can do better and try to move on." item.title: NFL announces course of action after latest Josh Jacobs allegations
item.description: Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) reacts after the game against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs opened the season on the NFL ’s commissioner exempt due to his arrest in May after being accused of throwing his then-girlfriend to the ground during a physical dispute in his garage. In September, Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal property damage. “Per the criminal complaint, a woman identified as Jacobs’ girlfriend told officers that she had been looking through Jacobs’ phone and saw that he was talking to other women. She became upset and threw his phone,” ESPN’s report read. “She told Jacobs he could look through her phone and told him to call a car to bring her to Chicago. When she tried to retrieve her phone, according to the complaint, Jacobs did not return it, grabbed her arm and began a physical struggle that lasted several minutes.” Things took another turn on Friday night when Jacobs was back in the headlines for another troubling reason. Per reports, after Jacobs’ initial arrest, multiple women have contacted the police to detail more alleged physical encounters with Jacobs. “According to the records, the woman alleged Jacobs slapped her across the face and later took the her cellphone as she attempted to leave his residence. The woman told investigators that Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down and later threw her onto the floor. The woman also alleged Jacobs spit on her and grabbed her by the throat,” NBC 26 reported. “The woman told police she initially met Jacobs through Instagram and communicated with him for approximately six months prior to meeting him in person. She said she remained friends with him for some time after the incident and did not want to report him.” On Saturday, the NFL announced its response to the new allegations that have surfaced. “We will review these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open,” the league announced, via Tom Pelissero. Jacobs has tallied 75 rushing yards and a touchdown on 32 carries across two games this season. At the time of this writing, the Packers have not released a statement. item.title: Brooks Koepka Exposes PGA Tour’s ‘Really Bad’ Rule Breach
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Brooks Koepka has pulled back the curtain on a dark corner of competitive golf, admitting he watched a severe rules violation go unpenalized during the current season. The five-time major champion revealed this week that he chose not to report the incident to officials, believing proof was impossible to secure. Speaking on Dan Rapaport’s Dan on Golf show, Koepka described the situation as “really bad” but noted that the player involved is not competing in the upcoming Skins Game. This revelation highlights a growing frustration among veterans who feel the current enforcement model leaves too much to chance. The core of the issue involves players improving their lies in the rough, a practice Koepka says happens frequently because they are rarely caught. “I’ve noticed a lot of guys do it, and guys get away with it more because you’re not on top of them,” Koepka explained. He described a scenario where a player might be in the left rough while another is hitting a shot, making it nearly impossible for a rules official to see every movement. Koepka continued, “So I might be over there hitting my shot, but you’re over here in the left rough and guys definitely do it, but it’s just how are you going to prove it?” According to Yahoo Sports , Koepka recalled a specific moment from the 2026 season where he had an unobstructed view of a chip shot. Despite witnessing what he called a “blatantly obvious” infraction, the American golfer decided against confrontation. This silence stems from a belief that the burden of proof is too high for playing partners. Koepka acknowledged that while he would speak up if an infraction were undeniable, the ambiguity of the rules creates a blind spot. The issue is not new, but the frequency has increased as players feel they can exploit the lack of cameras in the rough. At Royal Birkdale for the 2026 Open Championship, Koepka observed that even major players like Bryson DeChambeau incurred penalties, including a two-shot penalty. However, that visibility is the exception rather than the rule. item.title: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United: Rogers and Palmer strike as Martínez red card deepens United crisis
item.description: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United: Rogers and Palmer strike as Martínez red card deepens United crisis Chelsea returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, extending Michael Carrick’s side’s winless run to nine matches in all competitions. Morgan Rogers broke the deadlock shortly after half-time before Cole Palmer doubled Chelsea’s advantage from the penalty spot. United defender Lisandro Martínez was sent off for a second bookable offence following a VAR review, leaving the visitors with 10 men as Xabi Alonso’s side secured three points. As it happened Manchester United created the better opportunities in an entertaining first half. Captain Bruno Fernandes wasted a clear chance in the 19th minute, firing over after Bryan Mbeumo released him behind Chelsea’s defence. Chelsea thought they had taken the lead when Estêvão converted a rebound from Pedro Neto’s effort, but the Brazilian was flagged offside. United also had a goal ruled out in the 34th minute when Matheus Cunha turned in Harry Maguire’s header, only for VAR to confirm an offside infringement. United continued to threaten, with Amad Diallo forcing Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders into action before lifting another promising opportunity over the crossbar. At the other end, Chelsea came closest when Levi Colwill’s header deflected off Moisés Caicedo and struck the post. The breakthrough arrived five minutes after the restart. Chelsea midfielder Roméo Lavia won possession and released Rogers, who drove through United’s defence before calmly lifting the ball over Senne Lammens. United’s afternoon deteriorated when Martínez received his first booking in the 59th minute for pulling back Rogers. Four minutes later, the Argentine challenged Wesley Fofana inside the penalty area, prompting a VAR review. The referee awarded Chelsea a penalty and showed Martínez a second yellow card. Palmer stepped up in the 64th minute and converted despite Lammens getting a hand to his effort, giving Chelsea a two-goal advantage. The hosts almost added a third when Estêvão finished emphatically following Palmer’s pass, but another VAR review ruled the Brazilian offside. Lammens later denied him again with a sharp save. Manchester United nearly pulled one back in stoppage time when Mbeumo struck a powerful volley from the edge of the area, but Penders tipped the effort onto the crossbar. Chelsea comfortably saw out the remaining minutes to end their two-match losing streak, while another defeat increased the pressure on Carrick following United’s difficult start to the season.

item.title: That confirms it, it's all over for one star at Liverpool after 6 years
item.description: That confirms it, it's all over for one star at Liverpool after 6 years One Liverpool star looks like his time is up. The player all but confirmed that with his performance on Wednesday. Liverpool will naturally have some major decisions to make in 2027 as they continue their rebuild. In fact, there will be surprisingly many decisions, especially with a new sporting director in charge of things. Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, for instance - are they getting new contracts? We're really not sure as things stand and the Reds will have to find an answer to that one. Rio Ngumoha needs a new deal, too, while Alexis Mac Allister has been open about wanting to sign a contract with Liverpool. Whether they actually get around to offering him one is another matter. Neither of those are outright expiries in 2027, however. They'll simply enter the final year of their deals and necessitate either selling or renewing, we imagine. But there is one more contract expiry that looks ripe for a decision. Kostas Tsimikas's contract situation Kostas Tsimikas was something of a surprise return in the summer. Liverpool tried to sell him in 2025 but couldn’t find a buyer that the player agreed on. Instead, he went off on loan to AS Roma and endured a difficult season. Andy Robertson’s summer departure opened up a spot at left-back, though, and Liverpool wrestle happy for Tsimikas to take that backup role rather than sign someone new. However, his contract will expire next year. We feel it’s virtually impossible that he signs an extension, though. Tsimkas played the full 90 minutes against Chelsea on Wednesday in the EFL Cup but never found his groove. The Blues were able to attack space around him consistently - as shown by him bring straight dribbled past twice without actually winning a tackle on the day. His crossing was off, too. Only three of his 12 attempts found a red shirt, while his penalty miss extended the shoot-out beyond five rounds. It was simply a poor night but one in which Tsimikas had to prove himself as an adequate backup to Milos Kerkez. In fact, he likely has to show more than that as Liverpool aren’t 100 per cent set on Kerkez as their long-term option. That arguably works against Tsimikas. Liverpool won’t just want a pure backup but someone who could potentially rival and overhaul Kerkez for the role. Wednesday showed that the Greek won’t do that - he just isn’t consistent enough game to game. Couple that with being over 30 and there’s essentially zero chance that Liverpool renew Tsimikas’s contract next year.

item.title: Aston Villa Consider New Deal For This 32-Year-Old: Is A Two-Year Contract Sensible?
item.description: Aston Villa Consider New Deal For This 32-Year-Old: Is A Two-Year Contract Sensible? Aston Villa have built their midfield around control, energy and experience under Unai Emery, with Boubacar Kamara protecting the defence, Youri Tielemans directing possession and Amadou Onana adding physical strength. Ross Barkley offers something different, and that’s composure in tight spaces and the ability to help Villa manage matches when opponents increase the pressure. The 32-year-old has made 14 appearances across all competitions in 2026/27, scoring four goals and providing two assists. He has also made four Premier League starts, giving Emery another option during a demanding schedule that includes Champions League football. Although John McGinn provides further midfield cover, Barkley brings experience and composure that could prove valuable during the closing stages of tight matches. Villa can therefore assess his future without treating a new deal as an urgent recruitment need. His contribution has strengthened his case. Barkley can retain possession under pressure, connect short passing moves and help Villa protect a lead late in a match. Those qualities matter across a long campaign, particularly when Emery needs to rotate his regular starters without losing control in midfield. According to Football Insider , former Villa chief executive Keith Wyness believes the club could offer Barkley a two-year contract in the coming months. Wyness, who led Villa between 2016 and 2018, has suggested an appearance-based agreement with a lower basic wage and performance-related bonuses. Barkley’s continued usefulness makes that approach attractive. Villa could retain his experience without committing to a guaranteed starting role. Wyness praised the club for restoring the midfielder’s form and described the work as re-polishing a rough diamond. Should Aston Villa offer Barkley a performance-based contract? Appearance bonuses would link part of his earnings to availability, although they would not automatically guarantee compliance with Profit and Sustainability Rules; Villa must assess the full contract cost against their financial position. Emery needs experienced players who can close out tight European matches, and Barkley offers that option without demanding a guaranteed starting place. item.title: Malik Nabers Is Giants’ Only True Star Through Seven Weeks
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The New York Giants sit at 4-2-1 and hold first place in the NFC East, but the league awards tell a different story. No Giants offensive player appears in the national MVP or Offensive Player of the Year races. That silence ignores the hard truth: Malik Nabers is the best offensive player on the roster. Yahoo Sports reports that Nabers has played like the NFL’s best wide receiver over the past four weeks, even as the Giants switched starting quarterbacks from Jameis Winston to McCarthy. His 509 yards over that span lead all NFL receivers, a number that stands out even more given his lingering shoulder injury from Week 2. Just 13 months ago, Nabers tore his ACL and meniscus, yet most supporters overlook his current recovery while he plays through pain. He had one catch for a single yard in the lopsided loss to the Rams when that injury first flared up. Now he has 36 receptions in four games, second only to Puka Nacua across the entire league. The Giants offense would struggle to find its rhythm without him, especially with Jaxson Dart out for the season and J.J. McCarthy still finding his footing. The Rookie Who Plays Every Snap While Nabers gets the headlines, the offensive line deserves credit for keeping him upright. Ben Mauigoa has played every single offensive snap for the Giants this year, a feat matched only by Jon Runyan Jr. The rookie switched from tackle to guard and has allowed just one sack through his first seven games. He has only been flagged twice despite the constant pressure of a quarterback carousel. Yahoo Sports notes that Mauigoa is the pick for offensive rookie of the year over Malachi Fields, though Fields has stepped up as the clear second receiver. A Team Built on Grit and Depth The Giants have lost their top quarterback, their top edge rusher, and key defenders to injury, yet they still lead the division. Brian Burns, Braxton Berrios, and Tremaine Edmunds are all out, but the roster depth has held firm. Coach John Harbaugh admits the team needed the bye week to heal up before the stretch run. “It’s coming at the right time for us,” coach John Harbaugh said. “There are a lot of little nicks and bumps and bruises and strains and stresses on guys’ bodies that can use a little recovery time.” General Manager Joe Schoen says he likes the makeup of the team and the grit the players show. At his annual bye week news conference on Tuesday, general manager Joe Schoen informed reporters, “I’m happy where we are.” The ultimate goal remains winning the division, a topic Harbaugh says they discuss regularly. “We’ll bring it up every now and then,” Harbaugh said. “It’s definitely always forefront because that’s the ultimate goal.” With Nabers playing at an elite level and the team healthy enough to make a push, the Giants have earned their spot at the top of the NFC East.

The Tonga centre, formerly of Zebre, failed to overcome the blow to his left ankle suffered in defeat by Ospreys. The visitors from Parma were also hindered by the upcoming Nations Championship, with just one of their nine-strong Italy contingent, full-back Giovanni Montemauri, released for game time. It was Dragons that got the job done to avoid their inexperienced bench - which featured teenage Monmouth schoolboy Brogan Leary - being put under serious pressure in the closing stages. Tiatia's side can now reflect on a solid first block to the campaign, with the break for the November internationals a timely one given their stretched squad.
